messages:
mike (acme): Hey team, after rotating our API key we intermittently get invalid JSON back when using response_format strict json. Happens ~1-2% of requests. Some responses come back with Content-Type: text/html and an HTML error page embedded. alex (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal curl repro and the raw response body (no redaction needed for headers except the key)? mike (acme): Repro curl: ``` curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ -H 'Accept: application/json' \ https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/generate \ -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}], "response_format":{"type":"json","strict":true}}' ``` Raw response (one sample): ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 
Warning: upstream auth failed
Traceback...
``` That HTML breaks our JSON parser (we expect strict JSON). We also saw a 401 once right before the spike. alex (support): Thanks. From the headers it looks like the edge returned a 200 with HTML. Two quick asks: 1) can you share the X-Request-ID for one of the failed requests? 2) can you confirm whether you were retrying on 5xx from your side? mike (acme): X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d (one sample). We do exponential-retry on 502/504 only. No retries on 200. jamie (eng): Looping in eng. Initial hypothesis: an upstream auth page (HTML) is being cached/served for some requests when token rotation hits edge auth TTL. That can slip through if content-type enforcement on the edge isn't strict. Also check streaming/chunked responses — if stream got an HTML footer appended, strict parser fails. jamie (eng): @sre-bot can you grep edge logs for request_id r-0a1b2c3d and show the route + upstream status? sre-bot: Found 1 hit: route=/v1/chat/generate edge=lb-eu-2 upstream=auth-gateway status=200 upstream_status=401 cache_status=HIT Log excerpt: ``` [edge] incoming req r-0a1b2c3d auth=miss -> forwarded to auth-gateway [upstream] auth-gateway responded 401 with HTML login page [edge] cache HIT served cached body (HTML) with 200 to client (content-type text/html) ``` This explains HTML on 200. alex (support): That cache_hit on an auth 401 -> HTML landing page is the root cause. Two followups: 1) temporary mitigation: we can set a header to avoid cached HTML on your tenant (Cache-Control: no-cache) or 2) you can set Accept: application/json (we recommend both) as a client-side guard. mike (acme): We already set Accept: application/json in the curl above, but header capitalization may differ from some SDKs. We can add Cache-Control. jamie (eng): Longer-term fix: we'll add stricter content-type checking at the edge — if upstream returns HTML or content-type != application/json while response_format.strict is true, we should convert to 502 or strip cached HTML footers for streaming. Also adding a small server-side check to avoid serving cached auth-pages for authenticated routes. I'm opening ENG-3421 to track. lina (billing): Noted there was a billing spike from retries yesterday tied to this issue. We'll review and propose a partial credit for the affected window once engineering confirms the root cause window. alex (support): Workaround steps for you now: 1) include X-Request-ID on client requests (we can map faster), 2) add Cache-Control: no-cache and Ensure Accept: application/json exact header, 3) if you see HTML come back, do not parse — return 5xx to your caller and include the raw body to our support team. mike (acme): I added Cache-Control and forced the Accept header exact. After ~2000 requests the HTML cases dropped to 0.1%. Will keep monitoring. Thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup: jamie (eng): Thanks — we deployed a quick edge-rule to prevent caching auth-pages for tenant routes; ENG-3421 will include a content-type enforcement change and a test to cover streaming footers. alex (support): Closing loop — please DM me any new request IDs if you see failures. We'll keep ENG-3421 open until the fix is in prod. mike (acme): Will do, thanks all!
